This occupation inspects, diagnoses, adjusts, and repairs wind turbines, with maintenance covering electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic systems, and it is not a general term for all wind energy engineering or management jobs.

Troubleshoot pitch, variable speed, converter systems, and related component faults and diagnose the generator and control system; specific handling follows training, equipment, and the responsibility scope.

subject.name: Wind turbine technicians
subject.summary: The name wind turbine technician corresponds to the O*NET Wind Turbine Technician sample name and belongs to the same 49-9081 turbine service statistic, so no separate distribution is invented. The wind turbine technician corresponds to O*NET49-9081.00, inspecting, diagnosing, adjusting, and repairing wind turbines and handling electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic system faults. The tasks include routine maintenance, planned testing, spare parts management, and operating data collection, and may involve heights, small nacelles, and harsh weather. Wind farm engineering design, development, and continuous operations management are separated separately; knowledge and training, the corresponding work certificates, and unit site authorization cannot be replaced by a job title or a paper exercise.
